claim: Split benefit depends on the selected Full baseline and quality population.
population: 204 augmented splits; 21 Vendor and21 TRT Fulls reused
effect_denominator: both advantages Vendor142/204;TRT86/204; semantic+both reference_close80/140 and84/187
robustness: both signs persist in136/142 Vendor and86/86 TRT pairs over9 combinations; pooling flips0 signs
counterexample: ResNet/DeepX all19 splits have no Vendor energy benefit
allowed_wording: Observed benefit was conditional on baseline and admissible cohort.
too_strong_wording: Splitting generally makes accelerators faster and more efficient.

claim: Generic Top1 does not reliably reproduce the Native optimum in every group.
population: 21 exact augmented technical groups;204 split pairs
robustness: three large counterexamples fail Top1 in9/9 repeat combinations; reference_close retains them
counterexample: MobileNet/H8 Top1 correct in9/9 combinations; RegNet/DeepX likewise
allowed_wording: Selection transfer varied substantially across the observed exact groups.
too_strong_wording: Generic inference is useless or one vendor intrinsically causes rank reversal.

claim: Task completion changes proxy behavior without guaranteeing a better Top1.
population: 192 original common identities; nine classification groups have n17–20
robustness: exact original candidate set; excludes12 short augmentation precursors

claim: Nontrivial Generic shortlists help in most classification groups but retain severe counterexamples.
population: nine classification groups, n17–20;uniform k-subsets within each same group

claim: Throughput and energy optima often coincide but stable tradeoffs remain.
population: 21 exact split energy strata;204 splits;three repeats each
effect_denominator: same winner17/21;ResNet/DeepX fastest26.10% more J/task;energy winner24.57% less throughput
robustness: both ResNet winner identities stable3/3 and ranges separated; no median/pooling winner changes
counterexample: MobileNet/DeepX tiny0.172% energy difference with changing winners and overlapping ranges
allowed_wording: Stable group-specific tradeoffs prevent a universal throughput-only choice.
too_strong_wording: Inverse energy-throughput correlation independently proves better hardware efficiency.
